Match List I with List II :
List IList II
A. ProductivityI. Gross primary productivity minus respiration losses
B. Net primary productivityII. Rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers
C. Gross primary productivityIII. Rate of biomass production
D. Secondary productivityIV. Rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Productivity is defined as the rate of biomass production.

Gross primary productivity (GPP) of an ecosystem is the rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis.

Net primary productivity (NPP) is the gross primary productivity minus respiration losses ($R$), which is the available biomass for the consumption to heterotrophs.

Secondary productivity is defined as the rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers.

Therefore, the correct matching is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

Answer: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Which of the following statements are correct ?
(a) Energy flow from producers to consumers is unidirectional
(b) Energy pyramid can never be inverted
(c) Transfer of energy follows the 1% law
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Statement (a) is correct because energy flow in an ecosystem is strictly unidirectional, moving from producers to herbivores and then to carnivores. Energy cannot flow back in the reverse direction.

Statement (b) is correct because the pyramid of energy is always upright and can never be inverted. At each successive trophic level, a significant amount of energy is lost as heat to the environment.

Statement (c) is incorrect because the transfer of energy from one trophic level to the next follows the 10% law (Lindeman's law), not the 1% law. The 1% law applies only to the amount of incident solar radiation captured by plants (producers).

Therefore, only statements (a) and (b) are correct.

Answer: (a) and (b) only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Consider the pyramid of energy of an ecosystem given below:
If $T_4$ is equivalent to 1000 J , what is the value at $T_1$ ?
questions.solution:
According to the given pyramid of energy, if $\mathrm{T}_4$ is equivalent to 1000 J , then according to the 10 percent law, which states that only 10 percent of energy is transferred to each trophic level from the lower trophic level, the value at $\mathrm{T}_1$ is $10,00,000 \mathrm{~J}$.
$\begin{aligned} & T_1=10,00,000 \mathrm{~J} \\ & T_2=\frac{10}{100} \times 10,00,000=1,00,000 \mathrm{~J} \\ & T_3=\frac{10}{100} \times 100000=10,000 \mathrm{~J} \\ & T_4=\frac{10}{100} \times 10000=1000 \mathrm{~J}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: In an ecosystem if the Net Primary Productivity (NPP) of first trophic level is $100 x\left(\mathrm{kcal} \mathrm{m}^{-2}\right) \mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, what would be the GPP (Gross Primary Productivity) of the third trophic level of the same ecosystem?
questions.solution: NPP at first trophic level would be the GPP for second trophic level. NPP at second trophic level would be GPP for third trophic level. Therefore, $100 x\left(\mathrm{kcal} / \mathrm{m}^2 / \mathrm{yr}\right.$ ) would be GPP at second trophic level and $100 x \times 10 \%\left(\mathrm{kcal} / \mathrm{m}^2 / \mathrm{yr}\right)$ i.e., $10 x\left(\mathrm{kcal} / \mathrm{m}^2 / \mathrm{yr}\right)$ energy would be GPP at third trophic level.

questions.solution: In a food chain, producers (plants) form the first trophic level. The organisms that feed directly on these producers are called primary consumers. Parasites can occupy various trophic levels depending on their host.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Identify the correct statement:

A. Detrivores perform fragmentation.

B. The humus is further degraded by some microbes during mineralisation.

C. Water soluble inorganic nutrients go down into the soil and get precipitated by a process called leaching.

D. The detritus food chain begins with living organism.

E. Earthworms break down detritus into smaller particles by a process called catabolism.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Decomposition is one of the most important phenomena which recycles both organic and inorganic raw materials in the ecosystem. The decomposition forms a detritus food chain, which begins with dead and organic matters.

  • Detritivores (e.g., earthworm) break down detritus into smaller particles. This process is called fragmentation.
  • By the process of leaching, the water soluble inorganic nutrients go deep into the soil horizon and get precipitated as unavailable salts.
  • Bacterial and fungal enzymes degrade detritus into simpler inorganic substances. This process is called as catabolism.
  • Humification is the accumulation of a dark-coloured amorphous substance called humus which is highly resistant to microbial action and undergoes decomposition at an extremely slow rate.
  • The humus is further degraded by some microbes and release of inorganic nutrients occur by the process known as mineralisation.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Match the trophic levels with their correct species examples in grassland ecosystem.

(a) Fourth trophic level (i) Crow
(b) Second trophic level (ii) Vulture
(c) First trophic level (iii) Rabbit
(d) Third trophic level (iv) Grass

Select the correct option.
questions.solution:
a) Primary producers (PP): They are autotrophic organisms that fix up the solar energy and manufacture their own food from inorganic raw material. So, they form the base of the food chain constituting the first trophic level (T1). E.g. Grass

b) Primary consumers (PC) or Herbivores: There are animals that feed on green plants or plant products, so they constitute a second trophic level (T2). E.g. Rabbit

c) Secondary consumers (SC) or Primary carnivores: These are animals that feed on herbivores and form third level (T3). E.g. Crow

d) Tertiary consumers (TC) or Secondary carnivores: These are animal that feeds on secondary consumers constitute the fourth trophic level (T4). E.g. Vulture

questions.q: During ecological succession:
options: The establishment of a new biotic community is very fast in its primary phase.
The numbers and types of animals remain constant.
The changes lead to a community that is in near equilibrium with the environment and is called pioneer community.
The gradual and predictable change in species composition occurs in a given area.
questions.solution:
Ecological succession involves a gradual and fairly predictable change in the species composition of a given area, i.e., the numbers and types of animals. The establishment of a new biotic community is very slow in its primary phase.

The first set of species or community that develops in a bare area in ecological succession is the pioneer community. Pioneer species facilitate succession. The final steady stable self-sustaining community in an ecological succession that lead to a community that is in near equilibrium with the environment and is called climax community.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The rate of decomposition is faster in the ecosystem due to following factors $EXCEPT$:
options: Detritus richer in lignin and chitin
questions.solution:
The rate of decomposition of detritus is controlled by the chemical nature of detritus and a number of climatic factors given below.

  • Chemical nature of detritus: The decomposition of detritus is slow if it contains lignin, chitin, tannins (phenolics) and cellulose. It is rapid if detritus possesses more nitrogenous compounds (like proteins, nucleic acids) and water-soluble reserve carbohydrates or sugars.
  • The temperature above ${25}^{o}C$ favours the growth of microorganisms.
  • Soil moisture is the most important climatic factors that regulate decomposition through their effects on the activities of soil microbes.
  • Aeration: It is required for the activity of decomposers and detritivores. Reduced aeration will slow down the process of decomposition.
  • Soil pH: The growth of microbes is low in acidic soils as compared to basic soils.

So, the detritus rich in lignin and chitin will undergo slow decomposition.

What type of ecological pyramid would be obtained with following data?
Secondary consumer : 120 g
Primary consumer : 60 g
Primary producer : 10 g
questions.solution:
The inverted pyramid of biomass

Biomass is the amount of living material in an organism. The pyramids of biomass represent the relationship between different trophic levels in terms of biomass. In grassland and forest ecosystems, there is generally a gradual decrease in the biomass of organisms at successive trophic levels from the producers to the consumers. Their pyramid of biomass is upright. In an aquatic ecosystem, the producers are small organisms with the least biomass and the biomass gradually increase towards the apex of the pyramid. Thus, the pyramid of the biomass of aquatic ecosystems is inverted in shape.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: An association of individuals of different species living in the same habitat and having functional interactions is:
questions.solution:
Population: It is a grouping of individuals of the same species inhabiting a given area.

Biological Community: It is an assemblage of the population of different species present in an area which show interdependence and interaction like competition, predation, host-parasite, amensalism etc.

Ecosystem: It is composed of a biological community, integrated with its physical environment through the exchange of energy and recycling of the nutrients.

The ecological niche of organisms represents, the range of conditions that it can tolerate, the resource it utilizes and its functional role in the ecological system. Each species has a distinct niche and no two species are believed to occupy reproduction in its habitat through natural selection.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following statements is correct for secondary succession?
options: It occurs on a deforested site
It is similar to primary succession except that it has a relatively fast pace
It begins on a bare rock
questions.solution: Secondary succession or subsere is ecological succession that takes place in a recently denuded area which still contains a lot of organic debris, remains and propagules of previously living organisms. It is more common and caused by baring of an area due to forest fires, deforestation, excessive overgrazing, landslides, earthquakes, repeated floods, etc. Only 50 to 100 years are required for establishment of a grassland over a recently denuded area. Formation of forest requires 100 to 200 years.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Mass of living matter at a trophic level in an area at any time is called
questions.solution:
The amount of living matter present in an ecosystem in its different trophic levels is called standing crop. It is expressed in the form of number or biomass per unit area. Biomass is measured as either fresh weight or dry weight.
Dry weight is preferred over fresh weight as it is not liable to change with moisture content. Standing crop indicates the productivity and luxurience of growth.

questions.q: A renewable exhaustible natural resource is
questions.solution:
Forest is renewable, exhaustible natural resource. Renewable resources are living, able to reproduce or replace themselves and to increase. The renewable resources get replenished, recycled or reproduced and can fast forever provided they are not used beyond their renewability. Exhaustible resource are the natural resources with finite stock or supply, they are vulnerable to both qualitative and quantitative degradation.
Coal and petroleum are non-renewable and exhaustible natural resources.
Minerals are renewable and inexhaustible natural resources.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following representations shows the pyramid of numbers in a forest ecosystem?
questions.solution: Pyramid of number is spindle-shaped in a forest ecosystem because producers are mainly large trees which are less in number. Primary consumers like birds, deer, elephant, etc, are more in number than the producers, then the number of secondary consumers and tertiary or top consumers gradually decreases. Pyramid of number is inverted for parasitic food chain in a single tree ecosystem.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is a primary consumer in maize field ecosytem?
questions.solution:
Primary consumers are herbivorous organism, that feed on producers. In a food chain, grasshoppers are primary consumers, phytoplankton are producers, and wolf and lions are secondary and tertiary consumers respectively.
Related Theory
The amount of energy flow decrease with successive trophic levels as only $10 \%$ of energy is transferred from one trophic level to the next successive level. The energy is lost in the form of respiration and other vital activities to maintain life. If more trophic levels are present, the residual energy will be limited and decreased to such an extent that it cannot further support any trophic level by the flow of energy. So the food chain is generally limited to 3-4 trophic levels only.

(vi) Woodland stage, eg, Lantana, Salix, Populus, etc.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
A lake near a village suffered heavy mortality of fishes within a few days. Consider the following reasons for this
(1) Lots of urea and phosphate fertilizer were used in the crops in the vicinity.
(2) The area was sprayed with DDT by an aircraft.
(3) The lake water turned green and stinky.
(4) Phytoplankton populations in the lake declined initially thereby greatly reducing photosynthesis.
Which two of above were the main causes of fish mortality in the lake?
questions.solution:
The heavy mortality of fishes in the lake within a span of few days is due to Eutrophication.
Eutrophication is the phenomenon of nutrient enrichment of nitrogen and phosphorus in a water body that supports a dense growth of plants and animal life. Due to nutrient enrichment, excess growth of algae occurs which is called algal bloom. When these algae die, their organic matter gets decomposed and this results in the depletion of oxygen leading to death of aquatic animals. Hence, this indicates that lot of urea and phosphate fertilizers are were used in nearby crops. The lake water could have turned green and stinky due to excess growth of Algae.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: About $70 \%$ of total global carbon is found in
questions.solution: The atmosphere is the source of carbon dioxide, which is utilized by plants in photosynthesis reduced to form carbon compounds. The total mass of carbon currently in the atmosphere is about $7 \times 10^{17} \mathrm{~g}$, ie, 700000 million tonnes. Oceans regulate the $\mathrm{CO}_2$ content in the atmosphere and thus play a very important role. Sea water contains 50 times more $\mathrm{CO}_2$ than air, ie, about $70 \%$ of total global carbon is found in oceans. This is in the form of carbonates and bicarbonates.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Consider the following statements concerning food chains
A. removal of $80 \%$ tigers from an area resulted in greatly increased growth of vegetation
B. removal of most of the carnivores resulted in an increased population of deers
C. the length of food chains is generally limited to 3-4 trophic levels due to energy loss
D. the length of food chains may vary from 2 to 8 trophic levels
Which two of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution: The series of organisms eating one and being eaten by other is called food chain. A simple food chain consists of producers, herbivores and carnivores. The length of food chain is generally limited to 3-4 trophic levels due to energy loss. In grazing food chain the producers (ie, plants) are eaten by herbivores (ie, rabbit, deer, cow etc) and the herbivores are eaten by carnivores. Therefore, the removal of most of the carnivores resulted in an increased population of deers.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is not true for a species?
options: members of a species can interbreed
gene flow does not occur between the population of a species
each species is reproductively isolated from every other species
variations occur among members of a species.
questions.solution:
Gene flow is the "transfer" of genes from one population to another. This does happen between populations of a species, and tends to reduce the differences between populations. Gene flow occurs between populations of a species by gene migration i.e., emigration and immigration. This is because gene flow ensures that all the populations of a particular species share a common gene pool. Variations too, exist between members of a particular species.
Related Theory
In biology, species is the most basic unit of classification, as well as a taxonomic rank. The next taxonomic rank on the hierarchy of biological classification is a genus. Species is the lowest taxon in the taxonomical hierarchy. The members of a particular species can interbreed, but are reproductively isolated from members of other species.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: At which lattitude, heat gain through insolation approximately equals beat loss through terrestrial radiation?
questions.solution:
The latitude at which heat gain through insolation approximately equals heat loss through terrestrial radiation is at \(66^{\circ}\) North and South.
At these latitudes, near the poles, there is a balance between the heat received from the Sun (insolation) during the day and the heat radiated away from the Earth's surface during the night, resulting in a relatively stable temperature regime. This is one of the factors contributing to the formation of the polar climates.
So, the correct option is \((D): 66^{\circ}\) North and South

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The biomass available for consumption by the herbivores and the decomposers is called
questions.solution:
Net Primary Productivity (NPP) is the weight of organic matter stored by producers in a unit area/volume per unit time. NPP is equal to the rate of organic matter created by photosynthesis minus the rate of respiration and other loses. Stored biomass is transferred from one trophic level to another trophic level. Secondary Productivity is the rate of energy storage at consumers levels-herbivores, carnivorous and decomposers.
Gross Primary Productivity (GPP) is referred as total rate of photosynthesis including the organic matter used up in respiration during the measurement period.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Select the pairs of sedimentary biogeochemical cycles.
I. Hydrogen cycle and water cycle
II. Phosphorus Cycle and sulphur cycle
III. Calcium cycle and magnesium cycle
IV. Carbon cycle and nitrogen cycle
questions.solution:
Biogeochemical cycle is of two types:

Gaseous cycles: Exchange of nutrients occurs in gaseous or vapour form. In this cycle, biogeochemical is non-mineral and the reservoir pool is atmosphere or hydrosphere. E.g., Nitrogen, Carbon, Oxygen, Hydrogen cycle.

Sedimentary cycle: In this cycle, biogeochemical is mineral, reservoir pool is earth’s crust or lithosphere. E.g., sulphur, phosphorous, calcium and magnesium cycle.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Prolonged liberal irrigation of agricultural fields is likely to create the problem of:
questions.solution:
ace ground water contains salts to varying degrees, irrigation is the primary cause which brings salinity to the field.
Related Theory
Salinity and alkalinity problems are most likely to occur under 2 conditions:
(i) Intrusion of salt water into low-lying areas near oceans and seas.
(ii) Irrigated soils in semi-arid and arid regions (less than $500 \mathrm{~mm}$ annual rainfall) where rainfall or irrigation isn't sufficient to leach accumulated salts out of the root zone. The salts are released by decomposing rock and other parent material below the subsoil and are also brought in by irrigation water and additions of chemical fertilizers and manure.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: More than $70 \%$ of world's freshwater is contained in:
questions.solution: The distribution of water on the Earth's surface is extremely uneven. Only $3 \%$ of water on the surface is fresh; the remaining $97 \%$ resides in the ocean. Of freshwater, $69 \%$ resides in glaciers, $30 \%$ underground, and less than $1 \%$ is located in lakes, rivers, and swamps. Freshwater is water that contains little or no dissolved salt. Most freshwater is frozen in ice caps and glaciers.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is an ecosystem?
questions.solution: An ecosystem can be visualised as a functional unit of nature, where living organisms interact among themselves and also with the surrounding physical environment. Ecosystem varies greatly in size from a small pond to a large forest or a sea. Many ecologists regard the entire biosphere as a global ecosystem, as a composite of all local ecosystems on Earth. Since this system is too much big and complex to be studied at one time, it is convenient to divide it into two basic categories, namely the terrestrial and the aquatic. Forest, grassland and desert are some examples of terrestrial ecosystems; pond, lake, wetland, river and estuary are some examples of aquatic ecosystems. Crop fields and an aquarium may also be considered as man-made ecosystems.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is stratification in an ecosystem?
options: The vertical distribution of different species
The number of species in an ecosystem
The water component of an ecosystem
questions.solution: In earlier classes, you have looked at the various components of the environment- abiotic and biotic. You studied how the individual biotic and abiotic factors affected each other and their surrounding. Let us look at these components in a more integrated manner and see how the flow of energy takes place within these components of the ecosystem. Interaction of biotic and abiotic components result in a physical structure that is characteristic for each type of ecosystem. Identification and enumeration of plant and animal species of an ecosystem gives its species composition. Vertical distribution of different species occupying different levels is called stratification. For example, trees occupy top vertical strata or layer of a forest, shrubs the second and herbs and grasses occupy the bottom layers.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which ecosystem is a shallow water body and simple example of all four basic components of an ecosystem?
questions.solution: To understand the ethos of an aquatic ecosystem let us take a small pond as an example. This is fairly a self-sustainable unit and rather simple example that explain even the complex interactions that exist in an aquatic ecosystem. A pond is a shallow water body in which all the above mentioned four basic components of an ecosystem are well exhibited. The abiotic component is the water with all the dissolved inorganic and organic substances and the rich soil deposit at the bottom of the pond. The solar input, the cycle of temperature, day-length and other climatic conditions regulate the rate of function of the entire pond. The autotrophic components include the phytoplankton, some algae and the floating, submerged and marginal plants found at the edges. The consumers are represented by the zooplankton, the free swimming and bottom dwelling forms. The decomposers are the fungi, bacteria and flagellates especially abundant in the bottom of the pond. This system performs all the functions of any ecosystem and of the biosphere as a whole, i.e., conversion of inorganic into organic material with the help of the radiant energy of the sun by the autotrophs; consumption of the autotrophs by heterotrophs; decomposition and mineralisation of the dead matter to release them back for reuse by the autotrophs, these event are repeated over and over again. There is unidirectional movement of energy towards the higher trophic levels and its dissipation and loss as heat to the environment.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is the primary production in an ecosystem?
options: The rate of organic matter production in photosynthesis
The rate of new organic matter formation by consumers
The amount of energy produced by plants
questions.solution: A constant input of solar energy is the basic requirement for any ecosystem to function and sustain. Primary production is defined as the amount of biomass or organic matter produced per unit area over a time period by plants during photosynthesis. It is expressed in terms of weight (g m–2) or energy (kcal m–2). The rate of biomass production is called productivity. It is expressed in terms of gm–2 yr –1 or (kcal m–2) yr–1 to compare the productivity of different ecosystems. It can be divided into gross primary productivity (GPP) and net primary productivity (NPP). Gross primary productivity of an ecosystem is the rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis. A considerable amount of GPP is utilised by plants in respiration. Gross primary productivity minus respiration losses (R), is the net primary productivity (NPP). GPP – R = NPP Net primary productivity is the available biomass for the consumption to heterotrophs (herbiviores and decomposers). Secondary productivity is defined as the rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers. Primary productivity depends on the plant species inhabiting a particular area. It also depends on a variety of environmental factors, availability of nutrients and photosynthetic capacity of plants. Therefore, it varies in different types of ecosystems. The annual net primary productivity of the whole biosphere is approximately 170 billion tons (dry weight) of organic matter. Of this, despite occupying about 70 per cent of the surface, the productivity of the oceans are only 55 billion tons. Rest of course, is on land. Discuss the main reason for the low productivity of ocean with your teacher.

Gross primary productivity of an ecosystem is the rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis. A considerable amount of GPP is utilised by plants in respiration. Gross primary productivity minus respiration losses (R), is the net primary productivity (NPP). GPP – R = NPP Net primary productivity is the available biomass for the consumption to heterotrophs (herbiviores and decomposers). Secondary productivity is defined as the rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers. Primary productivity depends on the plant species inhabiting a particular area. It also depends on a variety of environmental factors, availability of nutrients and photosynthetic capacity of plants. Therefore, it varies in different types of ecosystems. The annual net primary productivity of the whole biosphere is approximately 170 billion tons (dry weight) of organic matter. Of this, despite occupying about 70 per cent of the surface, the productivity of the oceans are only 55 billion tons. Rest of course, is on land. questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is decomposition?
options: The process of breaking down organic matter into inorganic substances
The process of breaking down organic matter into water
The process of breaking down organic matter into nitrogen
The process of breaking down organic matter into humus
questions.solution:
Decomposition refers to the process of breaking down complex organic matter into inorganic substances like carbon dioxide, water and nutrients.

You may have heard of the earthworm being referred to as the farmer’s ‘friend’. This is so because they help in the breakdown of complex organic matter as well as in loosening of the soil. Similarly, decomposers break down complex organic matter into inorganic substances like carbon dioxide, water and nutrients and the process is called decomposition. Dead plant remains such as leaves, bark, flowers and dead remains of animals, including fecal matter, constitute detritus, which is the raw material for decomposition. The important steps in the process of decomposition are fragmentation, leaching, catabolism, humification and mineralization .Detritivores (e.g., earthworm) break down detritus into smaller particles. This process is called fragmentation. By the process of leaching, water- soluble inorganic nutrients go down into the soil horizon and get precipitated as unavailable salts. Bacterial and fungal enzymes degrade detritus into simpler inorganic substances. This process is called as catabolism. It is important to note that all the above steps in decomposition operate simultaneously on the detritus Humification and mineralisation occur during decomposition in the soil. Humification leads to accumulation of a dark coloured amorphous substance called humus that is highly resistant to microbial action and undergoes decomposition at an extremely slow rate. Being colloidal in nature it serves as a reservoir of nutrients. The humus is further degraded by some microbes and release of inorganic nutrients occur by the process known as mineralisation.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is the only source of energy for all ecosystems on Earth except the deep sea hydro:thermal ecosystem?
questions.solution: :. Except for the deep sea hydro-thermal ecosystem, sun is the only source of energy for all ecosystems on Earth. Of the incident solar radiation less than 50 per cent of it is photosynthetically active radiation (PAR). We know that plants and photosynthetic bacteria (autotrophs), fix Sun’s radiant energy to make food from simple inorganic materials. Plants capture only 2-10 per cent of the PAR and this small amount of energy sustains the entire living world. So, it is very important to know how the solar energy captured by plants flows through different organisms of an ecosystem. All organisms are dependent for their food on producers, either directly or indirectly. So you find unidirectional flow of energy from the sun to producers and then to consumers. Is this in keeping with the first law of thermodynamics?

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Do ecosystems need a constant supply of energy to maintain order?
questions.solution:
Ecosystems need a constant supply of energy to counteract the universal tendency toward increasing disorderliness as stated by the Second Law of Thermodynamics.

Further, ecosystems are not exempt from the Second Law of thermodynamics. They need a constant supply of energy to synthesise the molecules they require, to counteract the universal tendency toward increasing disorderliness.The green plant in the ecosystem are called producers. In a terrestrial ecosystem, major producers are herbaceous and woody plants. Likewise, producers in an aquatic ecosystem are various species like phytoplankton, algae and higher plants.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is the source of energy for all ecosystems on Earth, except for the deep sea hydro:thermal ecosystem?
questions.solution: Except for the deep sea hydro-thermal ecosystem, sun is the only source of energy for all ecosystems on Earth. Of the incident solar radiation less than 50 per cent of it is photosynthetically active radiation (PAR). We know that plants and photosynthetic bacteria (autotrophs), fix Sun’s radiant energy to make food from simple inorganic materials. Plants capture only 2-10 per cent of the PAR and this small amount of energy sustains the entire living world. So, it is very important to know how the solar energy captured by plants flows through different organisms of an ecosystem. All organisms are dependent for their food on producers, either directly or indirectly. So you find unidirectional flow of energy from the sun to producers and then to consumers. Is this in keeping with the first law of thermodynamics?

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What are animals that feed on herbivores called?
questions.solution: All animals depend on plants (directly or indirectly) for their food needs. They are hence called consumers and also heterotrophs. If they feed on the producers, the plants, they are called primary consumers, and if the animals eat other animals which in turn eat the plants (or their produce) they are called secondary consumers. Likewise, you could have tertiary consumers too. Obviously the primary consumers will be herbivores.Some common herbivores are insects, birds and mammals in terrestrial ecosystem and molluscs in aquatic ecosystem. The consumers that feed on these herbivores are carnivores, or more correctly primary carnivores (though secondary consumers). Those animals that depend on the primary carnivores for food are labelled secondary carnivores.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is the detritus food chain made up of?
questions.solution: The detritus food chain (DFC) begins with dead organic matter. It is made up of decomposers which are heterotrophic organisms, mainly fungi and bacteria. They meet their energy and nutrient requirements by degrading dead organic matter or detritus. These are also known as saprotrophs (sapro: to decompose). Decomposers secrete digestive enzymes that breakdown dead and waste materials into simple, inorganic materials, which are subsequently absorbed by them.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is the major conduit for energy flow in an aquatic ecosystem?
questions.solution: In an aquatic ecosystem, GFC is the major conduit for energy flow. As against this, in a terrestrial ecosystem, a much larger fraction of energy flows through the detritus food chain than through the GFC. Detritus food chain may be connected with the grazing food chain at some levels: some of the organisms of DFC are prey to the GFC animals, and in a natural ecosystem, some animals like cockroaches, crows, etc., are omnivores. These natural interconnection of food chains make it a food web. How would you classify human beings!

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is the trophic level of producers in a food chain?
questions.solution: Organisms occupy a place in the natural surroundings or in a community according to their feeding relationship with other organisms. Based on the source of their nutrition or food, organisms occupy a specific place in the food chain that is known as their trophic level. Producers belong to the first trophic level, herbivores (primary consumer) to the second and carnivores (secondary consumer) to the third

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What happens to the amount of energy at successive trophic levels?
questions.solution: The important point to note is that the amount of energy decreases at successive trophic levels. When any organism dies it is converted to detritus or dead biomass that serves as an energy source for decomposers. Organisms at each trophic level depend on those at the lower trophic level for their energy demands.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is the standing crop in a food chain?
options: The mass of living material at a particular time in a specific area
The amount of energy at a particular time in a specific area
The number of organisms at a particular time in a specific area
The biomass of a species in a specific area
questions.solution: Each trophic level has a certain mass of living material at a particular time called as the standing crop. The standing crop is measured as the mass of living organisms (biomass) or the number in a unit area. The biomass of a species is expressed in terms of fresh or dry weight. Measurement of biomass in terms of dry weight is more accurate. Why?The number of trophic levels in the grazing food chain is restricted as the transfer of energy follows 10 per cent law – only 10 per cent of the energy is transferred to each trophic level from the lower trophic level. In nature, it is possible to have so many levels – producer, herbivore, primary carnivore, secondary carnivore in the grazing food chain

questions.q: What is the base of an ecological pyramid representative of?
questions.solution: This, relationship is expressed in terms of number, biomass or energy. The base of each pyramid represents the producers or the first trophic level while the apex represents tertiary or top level consumer. The three types of ecological pyramids that are usually studied are (a) pyramid of number; (b) pyramid of biomass and (c) pyramid of energy.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What should be included in the calculations of energy content, biomass or numbers?
options: Only a few individuals at any trophic level
All organisms at that trophic level
questions.solution: Any calculations of energy content, biomass or numbers must include all organisms at that trophic level. No generalisations we make will be true if we take only a few individuals at any trophic level into account. Also a given organism may occupy more than one trophic level simultaneously. One must remember that the trophic level represents a functional level, not a species as such. A given species may occupy more than one trophic level in the same ecosystem at the same time; for example, a sparrow is a primary consumer when it eats seeds, fruits, peas, and a secondary consumer when it eats insects and worms. Can you work out how many trophic levels human beings function at in a food chain? In most ecosystems, all the pyramids, of number, of energy and biomass are upright, i.e., producers are more in number and biomass than the herbivores, and herbivores are more in number and biomass than the carnivores. Also energy at a lower trophic level is always more than at a higher level.

options: It takes into account the same species belonging to two or more trophic levels.
It assumes a simple food chain.
It gives saprophytes a place in the ecosystem.
questions.solution: However, there are certain limitations of ecological pyramids such as it does not take into account the same species belonging to two or more trophic levels. Moreover, saprophytes are not given any place in ecological pyramids even though they play a vital role in the ecosystem.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The pyramid of energy can be inverted in a marine ecosystem.
Reason (R): When energy flows from a particular trophic level to the next, some energy is always lost as heat at each step.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
The pyramid of energy is always upright and can never be inverted in any ecosystem, including marine ecosystems. This is because according to the 10 percent law and the second law of thermodynamics, when energy flows from a particular trophic level to the next, some energy is always lost as heat at each step. Therefore, the energy at a lower trophic level is always greater than at a higher level. Thus, the Assertion is incorrect, but the Reason is a correct statement.

Answer: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
In a grassland ecosystem, the grasses synthesize organic matter through photosynthesis and utilize a portion of it for their own metabolism. The remaining biomass is then consumed by a rabbit, which uses it to synthesize new organic matter for its own body.

Which of the following pairs of terms correctly identifies the remaining biomass in the grasses and the rate of formation of new organic matter by the rabbit, respectively?
options: Gross primary productivity and Secondary productivity
Secondary productivity and Net primary productivity
Net primary productivity and Secondary productivity
Net primary productivity and Gross primary productivity
questions.solution:
The total organic matter synthesized by the grasses is the Gross Primary Productivity (GPP). The portion utilized for their own metabolism is respiration loss (R). The remaining biomass ($GPP - R$) is the Net Primary Productivity (NPP), which is available to the next trophic level.

When the rabbit (a consumer) eats the grasses and forms new organic matter, this rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers is defined as Secondary productivity.

Answer: Net primary productivity and Secondary productivity

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In a grazing food chain consisting of Grass $\rightarrow$ Grasshopper $\rightarrow$ Frog $\rightarrow$ Snake, the energy available at the producer level is $5,00,000 \text{ J}$. What amount of energy will be available to the secondary consumer in this food chain?
questions.solution:
The given food chain is: Grass $\rightarrow$ Grasshopper $\rightarrow$ Frog $\rightarrow$ Snake.

Here, Grass is the producer (first trophic level, $T_1$).
Grasshopper is the primary consumer (second trophic level, $T_2$).
Frog is the secondary consumer (third trophic level, $T_3$).

Energy at the producer level ($T_1$) = $5,00,000 \text{ J}$.

According to Lindeman's 10% law, only 10% of the energy is transferred to the next trophic level.
Energy available to the primary consumer (Grasshopper) = 10% of $5,00,000 \text{ J} = 50,000 \text{ J}$.
Energy available to the secondary consumer (Frog) = 10% of $50,000 \text{ J} = 5,000 \text{ J}$.

Therefore, the energy available to the secondary consumer is $5,000 \text{ J}$.

Answer: $5,000 \text{ J}$

questions.q:
Consider the following food chain in a terrestrial ecosystem:

Grass $\rightarrow$ Grasshopper $\rightarrow$ Frog $\rightarrow$ Snake $\rightarrow$ Hawk

If $20,000\text{ J}$ of energy is available at the producer level, what will be the amount of energy available to the organism at the fourth trophic level?
questions.solution:
According to Lindeman's 10% law, only 10% of the energy is transferred from one trophic level to the next higher trophic level.

The given food chain can be mapped to trophic levels as follows:
First trophic level ($T_1$, Producer): Grass
Second trophic level ($T_2$, Primary Consumer): Grasshopper
Third trophic level ($T_3$, Secondary Consumer): Frog
Fourth trophic level ($T_4$, Tertiary Consumer): Snake
Fifth trophic level ($T_5$, Top Carnivore): Hawk

Energy available at $T_1$ (Grass) = $20,000\text{ J}$
Energy available at $T_2$ (Grasshopper) = 10% of $20,000\text{ J} = 2000\text{ J}$
Energy available at $T_3$ (Frog) = 10% of $2000\text{ J} = 200\text{ J}$
Energy available at $T_4$ (Snake) = 10% of $200\text{ J} = 20\text{ J}$

Therefore, the energy available at the fourth trophic level is $20\text{ J}$.

Answer: $20\text{ J}$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In an ecosystem, the net primary productivity (NPP) is always greater than the gross primary productivity (GPP).

Reason (R): A considerable amount of gross primary productivity is utilized by plants in respiration.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is true but Reason is false.
Assertion is false but Reason is true.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is false because gross primary productivity (GPP) is the total rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis, while net primary productivity (NPP) is the biomass remaining after respiratory losses (R) are deducted (NPP = GPP - R). Since respiration is always positive, GPP is always greater than NPP.

Reason (R) is true as plants utilize a considerable amount of the synthesized organic matter (GPP) for their own cellular respiration.

Therefore, Assertion is false but Reason is true.

Answer: Assertion is false but Reason is true.

questions.solution:
Statement A is correct: Humus is a dark-coloured amorphous substance that is highly resistant to microbial action and decomposes extremely slowly.

Statement B is incorrect: The degradation of humus by microbes to release inorganic nutrients is called mineralisation, not humification. Humification refers to the accumulation of humus.

Statement D is incorrect: The degradation of detritus into simpler inorganic substances by bacterial and fungal enzymes is called catabolism, whereas fragmentation is the physical breakdown of detritus by detritivores.

Therefore, only statements A and C are correct.

Answer: A and C only

The rate of formation of new organic matter by a herbivore (such as a rabbit) is called ___(X)___, and this process strictly depends on the ___(Y)___ of the producers.
options: X = Secondary productivity, Y = Gross primary productivity
X = Secondary productivity, Y = Net primary productivity
X = Net primary productivity, Y = Gross primary productivity
X = Gross primary productivity, Y = Net primary productivity
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, the rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers (heterotrophs) is defined as secondary productivity (X).

Therefore, X is secondary productivity and Y is net primary productivity.

Answer: X = Secondary productivity, Y = Net primary productivity

Finally, the humus is further degraded by some microbes and release of inorganic nutrients occurs by the process of mineralisation (D).

Thus, the correct sequence is C $\rightarrow$ E $\rightarrow$ B $\rightarrow$ A $\rightarrow$ D.

Therefore, only statements A, C, and E are correct.

questions.solution:
Productivity is defined as the rate of biomass production, which requires both an area and a time dimension. Hence, it is measured in $\mathrm{g \, m}^{-2} \, \mathrm{yr}^{-1}$ (A-II).

When standing crop is measured as a number, it is expressed as the number of individuals per unit area, such as Number $\mathrm{m}^{-2}$ (C-I).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
A sparrow can function as a primary consumer when it feeds on seeds, and as a secondary consumer when it feeds on herbivorous insects. Consider a crop field where the Net Primary Productivity (NPP) is $20,000\text{ J}$.

What will be the energy available to the sparrow when it feeds exclusively on the seeds (Case I) and when it feeds exclusively on the herbivorous insects (Case II), respectively?
questions.solution:
In Case I, the sparrow feeds on seeds, acting as a primary consumer (second trophic level, $T_2$).
Energy available at $T_1$ (NPP of crop) = $20,000\text{ J}$.
According to the 10 percent law, energy available to the sparrow = $10\%$ of $20,000\text{ J} = 2,000\text{ J}$.

In Case II, the sparrow feeds on herbivorous insects, acting as a secondary consumer (third trophic level, $T_3$).
Energy available to insects ($T_2$) = $10\%$ of $20,000\text{ J} = 2,000\text{ J}$.
Energy available to the sparrow ($T_3$) = $10\%$ of $2,000\text{ J} = 200\text{ J}$.

Therefore, the energy available in Case I and Case II is $2,000\text{ J}$ and $200\text{ J}$, respectively.

Answer: $2,000\text{ J}$ and $200\text{ J}$

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A considerable amount of organic matter produced during photosynthesis is utilized by plants for their own respiration. Which of the following correctly represents this utilized amount?
questions.solution:
Gross primary productivity (GPP) is the total rate of photosynthesis, but plants use some of this organic matter for their own respiration (R). The remaining biomass is the net primary productivity (NPP).

This relationship is given by the equation:
$\text{GPP} - \text{R} = \text{NPP}$

Rearranging this equation to solve for the respiratory loss (R) gives:
$\text{R} = \text{GPP} - \text{NPP}$

Secondary productivity refers to the formation of new organic matter by consumers, not the respiratory loss of plants.

Answer: $\text{GPP} - \text{NPP}$

questions.q:
Consider a simple grazing food chain: Grass $\rightarrow$ Grasshopper $\rightarrow$ Frog.

Which of the following accurately describes Net Primary Productivity (NPP) and Secondary Productivity in this specific scenario?
options: NPP is the rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis by the grass; Secondary productivity is the rate of formation of new organic matter by the frog only.
NPP is the grass biomass available to the grasshopper; Secondary productivity is the rate of formation of new organic matter by the grasshopper and the frog.
NPP is the grass biomass available to the grasshopper; Secondary productivity is the rate of formation of new organic matter by the frog only.
NPP is the rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis by the grass; Secondary productivity is the rate of formation of new organic matter by the grasshopper and the frog.
questions.solution:
In the given food chain, grass is the primary producer. Its Gross Primary Productivity (GPP) is the rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis.

Net Primary Productivity (NPP) is GPP minus respiration losses, which represents the grass biomass actually available to the primary consumer (the grasshopper).

Secondary productivity is defined as the rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers. In this chain, both the grasshopper (primary consumer) and the frog (secondary consumer) form new organic matter, meaning both contribute to secondary productivity.

Therefore, NPP is the grass biomass available to the grasshopper, and secondary productivity is the rate of formation of new organic matter by both the grasshopper and the frog.

Answer: NPP is the grass biomass available to the grasshopper; Secondary productivity is the rate of formation of new organic matter by the grasshopper and the frog.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Given below is a specific food chain in a terrestrial ecosystem:
Grass $\rightarrow$ Grasshopper $\rightarrow$ Frog $\rightarrow$ Snake $\rightarrow$ Hawk

If the Net Primary Productivity (NPP) of the Grass is $5000\text{ J}$, match the descriptions in List-I with their corresponding values in List-II.

List-IList-II
A. Energy available to FrogI. $5\text{ J}$
B. Energy available to SnakeII. $50\text{ J}$
C. Energy lost to the environment by GrasshopperIII. $500\text{ J}$
D. Energy available to HawkIV. $4500\text{ J}$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
The Net Primary Productivity (NPP) of the producers (Grass, 1st trophic level) is the energy available to the primary consumers (Grasshopper, 2nd trophic level). Thus, energy available to the Grasshopper is $5000\text{ J}$.

According to Lindeman's 10% law, only 10% of the energy available at one trophic level is passed on to the next. The remaining 90% is lost to the environment (through respiration, heat, etc.).

Energy available to Frog (3rd trophic level) = 10% of $5000\text{ J} = 500\text{ J}$. (Matches A to III)

Energy available to Snake (4th trophic level) = 10% of $500\text{ J} = 50\text{ J}$. (Matches B to II)

Energy available to Hawk (5th trophic level) = 10% of $50\text{ J} = 5\text{ J}$. (Matches D to I)

Energy lost to the environment by Grasshopper = Energy available to it $-$ Energy passed to Frog = $5000\text{ J} - 500\text{ J} = 4500\text{ J}$. (Matches C to IV)

Therefore, the correct matching is A-III, B-II, C-IV, D-I.

Answer: A-III, B-II, C-IV, D-I

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements carefully:
A. The unit of productivity can be expressed as $\text{g m}^{-2} \text{yr}^{-1}$.
B. Gross primary productivity is the available biomass for the consumption to heterotrophs.
C. Secondary productivity is defined as the rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers.
D. Net primary productivity minus respiration losses equals Gross primary productivity.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement A is correct. Productivity is the rate of biomass production, and it is expressed in terms of $\text{g m}^{-2} \text{yr}^{-1}$ or $(\text{kcal m}^{-2}) \text{yr}^{-1}$.

Statement B is incorrect. Net primary productivity (NPP), not gross primary productivity (GPP), is the available biomass for consumption by heterotrophs (herbivores and decomposers).

Statement C is correct. Secondary productivity is defined exactly as the rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers.

Statement D is incorrect. The correct relationship is GPP minus respiration losses (R) equals NPP (GPP - R = NPP). Therefore, GPP equals NPP + R, not NPP - R.

Exactly two statements (A and C) are correct.

Answer: Only two

Reason (R) correctly describes the process of leaching as stated in NCERT. Hence, (A) is not correct but (R) is correct.

Answer: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
In an aquatic ecosystem, the total rate at which solar energy is captured by phytoplankton during photosynthesis is reduced by the energy utilised for their own respiration. The remaining biomass, which is available for consumption by zooplankton, is termed as 'X' and is typically measured in units of 'Y'.

Select the correct option for X and Y.
options: X = Gross Primary Productivity ; Y = $\mathrm{g \, m}^{-2} \, \mathrm{yr}^{-1}$
X = Net Primary Productivity ; Y = $\mathrm{g \, m}^{-2}$
X = Net Primary Productivity ; Y = $\mathrm{kcal \, m}^{-2} \, \mathrm{yr}^{-1}$
questions.solution:
The total rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis is called Gross Primary Productivity (GPP).

A considerable amount of GPP is utilised by producers (phytoplankton) in respiration (R). The remaining biomass, which is available for consumption by heterotrophs (like zooplankton), is called Net Primary Productivity (NPP). Thus, NPP = GPP - R.

Since NPP is a rate of production (productivity), it must be expressed with both an area and a time dimension. Its standard units are $\mathrm{g \, m}^{-2} \, \mathrm{yr}^{-1}$ or $\mathrm{kcal \, m}^{-2} \, \mathrm{yr}^{-1}$.

The option with Y = $\mathrm{g \, m}^{-2}$ is incorrect because it lacks a time dimension and represents the unit for standing crop, not productivity.

Answer: X = Net Primary Productivity ; Y = $\mathrm{kcal \, m}^{-2} \, \mathrm{yr}^{-1}$

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In a typical aquatic food chain, which of the following organisms occupies the second trophic level?
questions.solution:
In an aquatic ecosystem, the grazing food chain typically follows this sequence:

Phytoplankton $\rightarrow$ Zooplankton $\rightarrow$ Small fishes $\rightarrow$ Large fishes

The first trophic level ($T_1$) is occupied by producers, which are the phytoplankton. The second trophic level ($T_2$) is occupied by primary consumers, which are the zooplankton. Small fishes act as secondary consumers and occupy the third trophic level ($T_3$), while large fishes act as tertiary consumers at the fourth trophic level ($T_4$).

Students often confuse the second trophic level with secondary consumers (small fishes), but the second trophic level always corresponds to primary consumers.

Answer: Zooplankton

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In a forest ecosystem, the Gross Primary Productivity (GPP) is $50,000 \text{ J m}^{-2} \text{ yr}^{-1}$. If the respiration losses (R) at the producer level are 20% of the GPP, what amount of energy will be available to the primary carnivores?
questions.solution:
Gross Primary Productivity (GPP) = $50,000 \text{ J m}^{-2} \text{ yr}^{-1}$.
Respiration losses (R) = 20% of GPP = $0.20 \times 50,000 = 10,000 \text{ J m}^{-2} \text{ yr}^{-1}$.

Net Primary Productivity (NPP) is the energy available to the first trophic level (producers).
$\text{NPP} = \text{GPP} - \text{R} = 50,000 - 10,000 = 40,000 \text{ J m}^{-2} \text{ yr}^{-1}$.

According to the 10% law of energy transfer:
Energy available to primary consumers (herbivores, $T_2$) = 10% of NPP = $4,000 \text{ J m}^{-2} \text{ yr}^{-1}$.
Energy available to primary carnivores (secondary consumers, $T_3$) = 10% of $4,000 = 400 \text{ J m}^{-2} \text{ yr}^{-1}$.

Thus, the energy available to the primary carnivores is $400 \text{ J m}^{-2} \text{ yr}^{-1}$.

Answer: $400 \text{ J m}^{-2} \text{ yr}^{-1}$

questions.q:
Read the following statements regarding trophic levels in an ecosystem.

Statement I: A given species can never occupy more than one trophic level in the same ecosystem at the same time.
Statement II: A sparrow acts as a primary consumer when it eats seeds, peas, or fruits.
Statement III: A sparrow acts as a secondary consumer when it eats insects and worms.
Statement IV: The trophic level represents a functional level, not a species as such.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement I is incorrect. According to NCERT, a given species may occupy more than one trophic level in the same ecosystem at the same time depending on its feeding choices.

Statement II is correct. When a sparrow eats plant products like seeds, peas, or fruits, it feeds directly on producers, acting as a primary consumer (second trophic level).

Statement III is correct. When a sparrow eats insects and worms (which are primary consumers), it acts as a secondary consumer (third trophic level).

Statement IV is correct. A trophic level represents a functional level based on the source of nutrition, not a specific species.

Therefore, exactly three statements (II, III, and IV) are correct.

Answer: Three

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In a grazing food chain, the primary producers have $10,000\text{ J}$ of available energy. If an organism 'X' in this food chain receives $1,000\text{ J}$ of energy transferred to its trophic level, what is the ecological role of organism 'X'?
questions.solution:
According to Lindeman's 10% law, only 10% of the energy is transferred from one trophic level to the next.

The primary producers (first trophic level) have $10,000\text{ J}$ of energy. The next trophic level will receive 10% of $10,000\text{ J}$, which is $1,000\text{ J}$.

Since organism 'X' receives $1,000\text{ J}$, it occupies the second trophic level. Organisms at the second trophic level feed directly on producers and are known as primary consumers (herbivores).

Answer: Primary consumer

Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In a terrestrial ecosystem, if the Net Primary Productivity (NPP) of the producers is $20,000\text{ J}$, the energy available to the tertiary consumers will be $20\text{ J}$.
Reason (R): According to the 10% law, only 10% of the energy is transferred from a lower trophic level to the next higher trophic level.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is false but Reason is true.
Assertion is true but Reason is false.
questions.solution:
The Net Primary Productivity (NPP) of the producers (1st trophic level) represents the total biomass available for consumption by the primary consumers (2nd trophic level). Therefore, the energy available to the primary consumers is $20,000\text{ J}$.

According to the 10% law, only 10% of the energy is transferred to each subsequent trophic level. The Reason statement correctly defines this law.

Applying the 10% law:
Energy available to secondary consumers (3rd trophic level) = 10% of $20,000\text{ J} = 2000\text{ J}$.
Energy available to tertiary consumers (4th trophic level) = 10% of $2000\text{ J} = 200\text{ J}$.

The Assertion claims the energy available to tertiary consumers is $20\text{ J}$, which is incorrect (it is $200\text{ J}$). A common mistake is to miscount the number of transfer steps or to take 10% of the producer's NPP to find the primary consumer's energy, which would incorrectly yield $20\text{ J}$ for the tertiary consumer. Thus, the Assertion is false, but the Reason is true.

Answer: Assertion is false but Reason is true.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Consider a specific food chain where a single large oak tree provides food for hundreds of caterpillars, which in turn support thousands of parasitic wasps. What will be the shape of the pyramid of numbers for this specific food chain?
questions.solution:
In this food chain, the producer is a single large tree, so the base of the pyramid of numbers is very narrow (number = 1). The primary consumers are hundreds of caterpillars, making the next trophic level wider. The secondary consumers are thousands of parasitic wasps, making the top level the widest. A pyramid that progresses from a narrow base to a progressively wider top is inverted.

A standard tree ecosystem with birds as secondary consumers would be spindle-shaped, and a grassland pyramid of numbers would be upright. The pyramid of energy is the one that is always upright.

Answer: Inverted

Assertion (A): To compare the productivity of different ecosystems, it is expressed in terms of $\mathrm{g} \mathrm{m}^{-2} \mathrm{yr}^{-1}$ or $(\mathrm{kcal} \mathrm{m}^{-2}) \mathrm{yr}^{-1}$.
Reason (R): Productivity is the rate of biomass production, whereas standing crop is the mass of living material present at a particular time.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is true but Reason is false.
Assertion is false but Reason is true.
Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true because productivity is expressed in units that include both area and time, such as $\mathrm{g} \mathrm{m}^{-2} \mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, to allow for comparison between different ecosystems.

Reason (R) is also true and correctly explains the Assertion. Productivity is defined as the rate of biomass production, which inherently requires a time dimension (per year). In contrast, standing crop is a static measurement of biomass at a specific time and is expressed without a time dimension (e.g., $\mathrm{g} \mathrm{m}^{-2}$). Therefore, the time component in the unit is necessary to represent the 'rate' aspect of productivity.

Answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
A researcher is constructing an ecological pyramid for a forest ecosystem but encounters a difficulty: a particular species of bird in the forest feeds on both plant seeds and herbivorous insects.

Which specific limitation of ecological pyramids is best highlighted by this difficulty?
options: Ecological pyramids do not accommodate a food web
It does not take into account the same species belonging to two or more trophic levels
It assumes a simple food chain, something that almost never exists in nature
Saprophytes are not given any place in ecological pyramids
questions.solution:
By feeding on plant seeds, the bird acts as a primary consumer (second trophic level). By feeding on herbivorous insects, the bird acts as a secondary consumer (third trophic level).

Ecological pyramids are constructed with each organism assigned to a single trophic level. The difficulty in placing this bird in the pyramid directly highlights the limitation that ecological pyramids do not take into account the same species belonging to two or more trophic levels.

Answer: It does not take into account the same species belonging to two or more trophic levels

questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct because bacterial and fungal enzymes degrade detritus into simpler inorganic substances through the process known as catabolism.

Reason (R) is incorrect because detritivores (like earthworms) perform fragmentation, which is the physical breakdown of detritus into smaller particles. They do not secrete the bacterial and fungal enzymes responsible for chemical breakdown (catabolism).

Answer: Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect

questions.q:
Read the following statements regarding the components of an ecosystem:
A. Standing state is the amount of inorganic nutrients present in the soil at any given time.
B. Standing crop is measured as the mass of living organisms or the number in a unit area.
C. The standing state of an ecosystem remains constant throughout the year.
D. Standing crop includes the detritus and non-living organic matter in the soil.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement A is correct: The amount of nutrients, such as carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus, and calcium, present in the soil at any given time is referred to as the standing state.

Statement D is incorrect: Standing crop strictly refers to the living organic matter (biomass) and does not include dead organic matter or detritus.

Therefore, exactly two statements (A and B) are correct.

Answer: Only two

questions.q: In a grassland ecosystem, a grasshopper feeds on living grass leaves while a fungus decomposes fallen dead leaves. The total rate of biomass production that serves as the available food source for both of these organisms is mathematically represented as:
questions.solution:
The grasshopper acts as a herbivore and the fungus acts as a decomposer. According to NCERT, Net Primary Productivity (NPP) is the available biomass for the consumption of heterotrophs, which includes both herbivores and decomposers.

NPP is calculated as Gross Primary Productivity (GPP) minus the respiration losses (R) of the producers. Therefore, the mathematical representation of the available food source for these organisms is GPP - R.

Answer: GPP - R

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In a grazing food chain, if the energy available to the tertiary consumer is $40 \text{ kJ}$, what is the Net Primary Productivity (NPP) of the producers in this ecosystem?
questions.solution:
In a grazing food chain, the trophic levels are arranged as follows:
Producers (1st trophic level) $\rightarrow$ Primary consumers (2nd trophic level) $\rightarrow$ Secondary consumers (3rd trophic level) $\rightarrow$ Tertiary consumers (4th trophic level).

According to Lindeman's 10% law, only 10% of the energy is transferred from one trophic level to the next.

Given that the energy available to the tertiary consumer (4th trophic level) is $40 \text{ kJ}$, we can calculate backward:
Energy at 3rd trophic level = $40 \text{ kJ} \times 10 = 400 \text{ kJ}$
Energy at 2nd trophic level = $400 \text{ kJ} \times 10 = 4,000 \text{ kJ}$

The energy available to the primary consumers (2nd trophic level) is exactly the Net Primary Productivity (NPP) of the producers. Therefore, the NPP of the producers is $4,000 \text{ kJ}$.

Misidentifying the tertiary consumer as the 3rd trophic level leads to $400 \text{ kJ}$, and adding an extra trophic level leads to $40,000 \text{ kJ}$.

Answer: $4,000 \text{ kJ}$

questions.solution:
The given value is $4500 \mathrm{g} \mathrm{m}^{-2}$, which represents biomass per unit area but lacks a time dimension (such as $\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$).

Productivity (whether gross primary, net primary, or secondary) is the rate of biomass production and must include a time component in its unit (e.g., $\mathrm{g} \mathrm{m}^{-2} \mathrm{yr}^{-1}$).

Standing crop is defined as the mass of living material (biomass) at a particular time in a unit area, and it is measured in units like $\mathrm{g} \mathrm{m}^{-2}$. Therefore, the reported value represents the standing crop.

Answer: Standing crop

Assertion (A): In a grazing food chain, primary carnivores occupy the third trophic level.
Reason (R): Herbivores, which feed directly on producers, occupy the second trophic level.

Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.solution:

Reason (R) is true: Herbivores are primary consumers that eat producers, placing them at the second trophic level.

The Reason correctly explains the Assertion because the sequential numbering of trophic levels means the position of primary carnivores (third trophic level) is a direct consequence of their prey (herbivores) occupying the second trophic level.

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
In an aquatic ecosystem, a small standing crop of phytoplankton supports a large standing crop of zooplankton.

Which of the following ecological pyramids is best described by this statement?
questions.solution:
The standing crop of a trophic level can be measured as the number of organisms or their biomass. In an aquatic ecosystem, the number of phytoplankton is vastly greater than the number of zooplankton, meaning the pyramid of numbers is upright.

However, because phytoplankton are microscopic and have a very rapid turnover rate, their total mass (biomass) at any given time is smaller than the biomass of the zooplankton they support. Therefore, a "small standing crop supporting a large standing crop" in this context refers to biomass, which results in an inverted pyramid of biomass.

The pyramid of energy is always upright and can never be inverted.

Answer: Inverted pyramid of biomass

$\text{GPP} = 1\% \text{ of } 2,000,000 \text{ J} = 20,000 \text{ J}$

Net Primary Productivity (NPP) is the energy remaining after respiratory losses (R).
$\text{R} = 20\% \text{ of } 20,000 \text{ J} = 4,000 \text{ J}$
$\text{NPP} = \text{GPP} - \text{R} = 20,000 \text{ J} - 4,000 \text{ J} = 16,000 \text{ J}$

The NPP is the energy available to the primary consumers (2nd trophic level).
According to the 10% law, the energy available to the secondary consumers (3rd trophic level) will be 10% of the energy available to the primary consumers.
Energy for secondary consumers = $10\% \text{ of } 16,000 \text{ J} = 1,600 \text{ J}$.

Forgetting to subtract respiratory loss leads to $2,000 \text{ J}$, while calculating for the primary consumer gives $16,000 \text{ J}$.

Answer: $1,600 \text{ J}$

$\text{NPP} = \text{GPP} - \text{R} = 20,000 \text{ J} - 4,000 \text{ J} = 16,000 \text{ J}$

The NPP is the energy available to the primary consumers (2nd trophic level).

Energy for secondary consumers = $10\% \text{ of } 16,000 \text{ J} = 1,600 \text{ J}$.

Answer: $1,600 \text{ J}$

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Most animals that live in deep oceanic waters are
questions.solution: Benthos is the community of organisms which live on, in, or near the sea bed, also known as the benthic zone. As no light is available in this zone of sea, the energy source for deep benthic ecosystem is often organic matter from higher water column which drifts down to the depths. This dead and decaying matter sustains the benthic organisms, and therefore, most organisms in benthic zone i.e., in deep oceanic waters, are scavengers or detritivores.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Assertion : Rice field is an ecosystem for plants and animals.
Reason : Gut of human/animals is an ecosystem for flora and fauna.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false
questions.solution:
The human digestive system carries about trillions of microorganisms colonising the gut making an amazing ecosystem that live together in harmony. In this context human intestine is said to be rich in flora and fauna. The microorganisms perform a host of useful functions, such as fermenting unused energy substrates, training the immune system, preventing growth of harmful, pathogenic bacteria, regulating the development of the gut, producing vitamins for the host (such as biotin and vitamin $\mathrm{K}$ ), and producing hormones to direct the host to store fats.
Fish culture is sometimes done in combination with a rice crop, so that fish are grown in the water in the paddy field. Thus, a rice field is an example of ecosystem inhabiting both plants and animals.

questions.solution: There are two types of food chains: grazing food chain and detritus food chain. Detritus food chains are those which start from the dead bodies of animals or fallen leaves etc. In terrestrial ecosystems, detritus food chain is the major conduit of energy flow, while in aquatic ecosystems, grazing food chain is the major conduit of energy flow. As the detritus food chains depend upon the dead organic matter hence, these are not directly dependent upon solar energy.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is the Greek word for ecology?
questions.solution: The term ecology was coined by combining two Greek words, oikos (meaning 'house' or 'dwelling place') and logos (meaning 'the study of') to denote such relationships between the organisms and their environment. Thus, literally, ecology is the study of organisms 'at home'.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Animals take phosphorus from
questions.solution: Phosphorus is a major constituent of biological membranes, nucleic acids and cellular energy transfer systems. Many animals also need large quantities of this element to make shells, bones and teeth. The natural reservoir of phosphorus is rock, which contains phosphorus in the form of phosphates. When rocks are weathered, minute amounts of these phosphates dissolve in soil solution and are absorbed by the roots of the plants. Herbivores and other animals obtain this element from plants.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Assertion : Secondary succession takes place in recently denuded area.
Reason : It is caused due to baring of an area.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution: Biotic or ecological succession is the formation of a series of biotic communities at the same site over a period of time one after the other, till a stable climax community develops over the area. It occurs generally in bare areas. Primary succession takes place on a biological sterile soilless primary barren area. Secondary succession takes place in a recently denuded area which still contains a lot of organic debris, remains and propagules of previous living organisms. The area has become bared due to destruction of the community previously present. The baring of an area can be caused due to forest fire, deforestation for wood, timber and habitat, overgrazing, landslides or earthquakes, excessive and repeated droughts, fallowing a cropland and repeated floods.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The bacteria which attack dead animals are
options: first link of the food chain and are known as primary producers
second link of the food chain and are herbivorous
third link of the food chain and are tertiary consumers
the end of food chain and are decomposers.
questions.solution: Bacteria attacking the dead animals represent the end of the food chain and are decomposers. These are the organisms that obtain energy from chemical breakdown of organisms. They secrete enzymes onto dead matter and then absorb the breakdown products. Bacteria are specialised to breakdown organic materials that are difficult for other organisms to digest. They also fulfil a vital role in the ecosystem, returning the constituents of organic matter to the environment in inorganic forms so that they can again be assimilated by producers.

questions.solution: Net primary productivity is the available biomass for the consumption to heterotrophs (herbivores and decomposers). The rate of biomass production is called productivity. It has two aspects, gross primary productivity and net primary productivity. The rate of total production of organic matter during photosynthesis is known as gross primary productivity. Its considerable amount is utilised by plants in respiration. The organic matter synthesised by plants (GPP) minus the rate of respiration and other loss represents the net primary productivity.

questions.solution: Organic sulphur is made available to the plant through biological oxidation through the activity of certain microorganisms. Sulphur is transformed from the organic form to the sulfate ion, the form of sulphur that higher plants absorb. Soil microorganisms oxidize not only organic sulphur but also sulphide minerals such as ferrous sulphide. The elemental sulphur is then oxidized to sulphate by sulphur bacteria.

questions.q:
Assertion : Deforestation is one main factor contributing to global warming.
Reason : Besides $\mathrm{CO}_2$, two other gases methane and CFCs are also included under green house gases.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of the assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion
If assertion is true, but reason is false
Both assertion and reason are false statements.
questions.solution:
Deforestation increases atmospheric $\mathrm{CO}_2$ content by releasing carbon stored in organic matter and reduced primary productivity. So deforestation is one of the main factors contributing to global
warming other than green house gases. The various green house gases are $\mathrm{CO}_2(60 \%$ warming effect), $\mathrm{CH}_4$ (20\% warming effect) CFC ( $14 \%$ warming effect) and nitrogen oxide $\left(\mathrm{N}_2 \mathrm{O}, 6 \%\right.$ warming effect). Due to increase of $\mathrm{CO}_2$ concentration, the absorption of heat radiation also increase thus increasing the temperature. This increase in temperature may causes melting of glacier and polar ice caps, which is called global warming. This melting of glaciers and polar ice results in raising the sea level. Actually these green house gases absorbs infra red radiations (heat) of the sun like glass and thus traps the heat and does not allow it to radiate back to the space. They instead radiate the heat back to earth, thus causing increase in temperature.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Assertion : UV radiation causes photodissociation of ozone into $\mathrm{O}_2$ and $\mathrm{O}$, thus causing damage to the stratospheric ozone layer.
Reason : Ozone hole is resulting in global warming and climate change.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of the assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion
If assertion is true, but reason is false
Both assertion and reason are false statements.
questions.solution: Stratosphere zone of earth's atmosphere contains a layer of ozone  $\left(\mathrm{O}_3\right)$ which prevents the earth surface from about $99 \%$ of incoming solar ultra violet radiations. The primary chemicals responsible for ozone depletion are a group of chlorine containing compounds called chloroflourocarbons (CFCs) used as coolants in refrigerators and air conditioners and propellants for aerosol cans and foam blowing agents for insulation and packaging and also as solvents. After their release into troposphere CFCs go to stratosphere when these are broken down by ultraviolet radiations releasing chlorine or bromine which break $\mathrm{O}_3$ molecules into $\mathrm{O}_2$ and $\mathrm{O}$. Due to depletion of $\mathrm{O}_3$ layer, higher levels of ultra violet rays reach earth surface. Depletion in the concentration of ozone over a restricted area is called ozone hole. Ozone depletions results in problems like skin cancer, cataract animals becoming blind, mutations, inhibiting photosynthesis, decreases in productivity. Decreased photosynthetic activity will increase $\mathrm{O}_2$ concentration of the atmosphere resulting in global warming. Besides $\mathrm{CFCs}$, nitrogen oxide and hydrocarbons are also responsible for $\mathrm{O}_3$ depletion.

questions.solution: A cross section of well developed soil shows more or less distinct layers called horizons. Ohorizon is the topmost layer of soil and A-horizon comes below O horizon. In the topmost layer, vegetation grows and various biological activities takes place. Tropical rain forests are found in tropical zone of the world and are characterized by very high temperature and abundance of rainfall. Soil in these area are red latosols and are exceedingly thick. Leaching of minerals from the top soil occurs rapidly but cycling of nutrients also occur here. The laterite soils are generally infertile because of intensive leaching and not due to growth of micro-organism.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of terms / names mean one and the same thing?
questions.solution:
Gene pool is the total gene present in a population. Genome is the total genetic constitution of an organism. Codon is the basic unit of genetic code, a sequence of three adjacent nucleotide in DNA or $m$ RNA that code for an amino acid. Gene is the basic unit of heredity, a sequence of DNA nucleotide that encodes a protein.
Cistron is a segment of DNA nucleotides that codes for a polypeptide chain. Triplet is a three nucleotides sequence coding for an amino acid.
Therefore,

$\begin{aligned}$& $\text{ codon } \approx \text{ triplet }$\\
& $\text{ cistron } \approx \text{ gene }
\end{aligned}$DNA fingerprinting is technically called DNA profiling or DNA typing.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Intermediate community between pioneer and climax communities is called
questions.solution: The first biotic community which develops in a bare area is called pioneer community. The various biotic communities that develop during biotic succession are termed as seral or transitional communities.
